The most common blood type is **O positive (O+)** [d1][d2][d3][d8]. According to the American Red Cross, approximately 38% of the population has O positive blood, making it the most common blood type globally [d3][d4][d5]. In the United States specifically, O positive is confirmed as the most common blood type, with the Cleveland Clinic and Medical News Today both citing this figure [d2][d8]. The NHS notes that in the UK, blood group O broadly (including both O+ and O−) is the most common, with nearly 48% of the UK population falling into this group [d6]. Stanford Blood Center similarly reports that 37.4% of the US population has type O+, reinforcing its status as the most common and most transfused blood type [d7].
